character_facts: The man has significant mechanical augmentation, visibly including part of the face and a hand.
The man carries deep resentment over believing his mother was dead for years.
The woman presents herself as having concealed her existence intentionally for strategic reasons.
The woman appears calm, controlled, and unapologetically manipulative in explaining her choices.
The woman is linked to the man through his childhood and to his father through her account of foreseeing his death.
characters_present: Angry male figure with a mechanical lower face/hand and, per dialogue, a mechanical heart
Woman with long pale hair dressed in black, calm and seated, speaking as if she hid her existence
continuity_links: This page refers back to an earlier period when the man was a child and believed his mother was dead.
It also refers to an earlier incident involving the father's lung injury and predicted death.
The dialogue connects the man's lifelong suffering and revenge to a larger plan culminating in the destruction of 'Shabda-Oud.'
dialogue_meaning: The exchange is a confrontation over long absence, secrecy, and emotional harm.
The woman justifies hiding herself by saying open emotion or knowledge of her survival would have exposed them to hostile pursuers.
She claims she deliberately preserved the man's hatred and grief because those emotions were required to drive him toward a destructive mission against 'Shabda-Oud.'
The man rejects this justification and frames his childhood belief that his mother was dead as prolonged agony.
The woman treats the man's current cyborg state as distancing him from ordinary human suffering and urges him to leave with her.
locations: Interior of a blue, organic or biomechanical room, likely aboard a ship
A spacecraft shown in an inset panel, identified by dialogue as the woman's ship
lore_facts: The woman possesses some form of psychic or precognitive sensing, described as a 'psychic sonar.'
The man's father had injured lungs and was expected to die.
There are hostile 'beasts' capable of detecting emotions and wiping people out if alerted.
'Shabda-Oud' is a target the man was expected to exterminate.
The man has a mechanical heart.
The woman has access to a ship and invites the man aboard it.
plot_events: A man accuses the woman of abandoning him for roughly ten years and causing suffering.
The woman explains that she foresaw the death of the man's father and intervened because his lungs were injured.
She says the man had to remain alive despite that intervention.
The man says believing his mother was dead made his life a continual torment.
The woman argues that a child part of him still survived inside him, while an adult self had to hear and conceal her existence.
She says strong emotions would have exposed them to enemies, who would have detected and destroyed them.
She says it was necessary for him to keep his hatred and desire for revenge so that he would destroy the 'Shabda-Oud' himself.
The woman concludes that he now has a mechanical heart and therefore does not understand suffering, and she invites him to come with her to her ship.
uncertainties: The exact names of the man, the woman, and the father are not given on this page.
The precise spelling and nature of 'Shabda-Oud' are uncertain because it is read from small dialogue text.
The exact identity of the 'beasts' and the full mechanics of the woman's 'psychic sonar' are not explained on this page.
The room appears to be inside a ship or organic structure, but the page does not explicitly label the location until the final invitation to 'my ship'.
visual_summary: A tense conversation unfolds inside a blue-toned, organic-looking room or ship interior. A furious man with a metallic lower face and a mechanical hand confronts a seated woman in black with long pale hair. He crouches near her, then leans in angrily in close-up panels. The woman remains composed and explanatory. A later panel shows her hand on or near the top of his head, where a spiral-like device or mechanical feature is visible. The page ends with a small spacecraft image between dialogue boxes and another close-up of the man's enraged face.
